CONSULAAT-GENERAAL DER NEDERLANDEN
VOOR MIDDEN-CHINA.
TEL. AD. HOLLANDIA.
No. 3583.

SHANGHAI, 23rd October 1931.

〔此处转录不清：右上角印章及手写编号 No ... 2762 / 24. 10. 31.〕

Sir,

I have the honour to acknowledge the receipt
of your letter of 19 October 1931, S.P.-D.2762, con-
cerning a certain Amat Pakal and in connection there-
with wish to state that no member of the staff has
given "permission" for this man to be detained in the
Police Station. From the very beginning this Consulate
General wished to avoid determining the question of
his nationality as no definite data were available to
decide this issue and when the question of providing
Pakal with quarters and food cropped up, he was simply
asked whether he had any objection to staying in the
Station to which he answered that he had none. He
stayed there of his own free will and there existed no
objections on the part of this Consulate General to
this course, but to infer from this that "permission"
was given would not be an altogether correct statement
of the facts.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

〔此处转录不清：手写签名〕
Consul-General.

〔此处转录不清：左侧手写批注 His / R... / 23/10 HR. 24/10〕

Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
SHANGHAI.

荷兰驻华中总领事馆
电报挂号：HOLLANDIA。
第 3583 号。

上海，1931年10月23日。

〔此处转录不清：右上角印章及手写编号 No ... 2762 / 24. 10. 31.〕

先生：

谨此确认收到阁下1931年10月19日来函（S.P.-D.2762），内容涉及一名名为 Amat Pakal 的男子。就此事宜，本人愿声明，本馆任何职员均未给予“许可”将该人拘押于巡捕房。自始至终，本总领事馆均希望避免判定其国籍问题，因缺乏确凿资料以决定此事；而当提出为 Pakal 提供食宿的问题时，仅询问他是否反对留在巡捕房，他回答并无异议。他是出于自愿留在那里的，本总领事馆对此做法并无异议，但若据此推断已给予“许可”，则对事实的陈述并不完全准确。

谨致
敬礼，

〔此处转录不清：手写签名〕
总领事。

〔此处转录不清：左侧手写批注 His / R... / 23/10 HR. 24/10〕

R.M.J. Martin 先生，
警务处处长，
上海工部局，
上海。

Sir,

I have the honour to acknowledge receipt of
your letter No. 3447 of October on the subject of
the repatriation of a certain Amat Pakal.

I much regret that the correspondence emanating
from this office should have given the erroneous im-

individual. This impression was based on verbal per-
mission given by a member of your staff for the temporary
detention of Amat Pakal in the Police Station. The
error is much regretted and the correct position has
been duly noted.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,

先生：

谨此确认收到阁下10月份关于遣返一名名为 Amat Pakal 男子的第 3447 号来函。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C.I.D. S.B. D. 276 File No. Date 17 - 10 - 31 Section 2. SANSON）

REPORT

Date October 17, 1931.

Subject (in full) Amat Pakal.

Made by D.S. Moore.    Forwarded by （签名）

Re: the attached letter from the Netherlands Consul-General
denying that he accepted jurisdiction over the above named native
of Sumatra after he arrived in this city from Tientsin on September
21st 1931.
Amat Pakal was taken from the s.s. "Fau Sang" by D.S.
Sansom and interviewed by Mr. Van den Berg on September 22nd.
At this interview, Amat Pakal was interrogated by Mr. Van den Berg,
at the conclusion of which Mr. Van den Berg informed D.S. Sansom
that he would arrange for Amat Pakal to be sent to Sumatra by the
first available steamer and that in the meantime he gave the
Police the authority to keep Amat Pakal at a Police Station and
requesting the Police to make arrangements for Amat Pakal's
clothing to be washed. The authority to keep Amat Pakal at a
Police Station until the ship sailed was verbal, but by virtue of
the instructions issued by Mr. Van den Berg, D.S. Sansom gained
the impression that the Netherlands Authorities were accepting
jurisdiction over the man concerned and included these words in
his report of September 22nd 1931.

（签名：D.S. Moore D.S.）

Officer i/c Special Branch.
Commissioner of Police,
For Information
（签名：N. Lydimo O./c Sp. B. 17:10:31）

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 刑事侦缉处 特别分部 D. 276 档案号 日期 17 - 10 - 31 第 2 科. SANSON）

报告

日期：1931年10月17日。

主题（全称）：Amat Pakal。

制作人：D.S. Moore。    转呈人 （签名）

事由：附呈荷兰总领事来信，否认其在上述苏门答腊土著于1931年9月21日从天津抵达本市后接受对其行使管辖权。
Amat Pakal 由 D.S. Sansom 从“Fau Sang”轮带下，并于9月22日由 Van den Berg 先生进行问话。
在此次问话中，Van den Berg 先生讯问了 Amat Pakal，结束时 Van den Berg 先生告知 D.S. Sansom，他将安排 Amat Pakal 搭乘第一班可用的轮船前往苏门答腊，同时授权警方将 Amat Pakal 拘押在巡捕房，并请警方安排清洗 Amat Pakal 的衣物。将 Amat Pakal 拘押在巡捕房直至轮船启航的授权是口头的，但基于 Van den Berg 先生发出的指示，D.S. Sansom 产生了一种印象，即荷兰当局正在接受对该人的管辖权，并在其1931年9月22日的报告中写入了这些措辞。

（签名：D.S. Moore D.S.）

特别分部主管警官。
警务处处长，
供阅知
（签名：N. Lydimo O./c Sp. B. 17:10:31）

CONSULAAT-GENERAAL DER NEDERLANDEN
VOOR MIDDEN-CHINA.
TEL. AD. HOLLANDIA.

No. 3447. SHANGHAI, 14th October 1931.

（批：* Sir,
File attached
〔此处转录不清〕）

（印：... U.S. ... B. D. 2762. 15 - 10 - 31.）

Sir,

I have the honour to inform you that from correspon-
dence submitted by the Netherlands Consulate at Tientsin
concerning the repatriation of a certain Amat Pakal alias
Doela Sanin, it appears that the Shanghai Municipal Council
are under the impression that I assumed jurisdiction over
this person. In connection therewith I desire to make it
clear that from the very beginning I have refused to do so
and that my interest in this man only confined itself to an
inquiry with the local management of the Java China Japan
Line as to whether they could take this man on board of one
their steamers and bring him nearer home. This they were pre-
pared to do and there is no question of my having ever ordered
Amat Pakal to be repatriated. He left voluntarily at my
suggestion. As you will see from the copy of the letter of
Mr. Isemonger to Mr. Snyers, which is enclosed herewith, the
British Municipal Council at Tientsin would be glad to receive
back the full amount of the expenses incurred there on this
man's account.

The Netherlands Benevolent Society at Shanghai was pre-
pared to contribute, on the understanding that this would not
prejudice the man's nationality, a sum of $ 20.--, which
were remitted by me to Tientsin, to reimburse those private
persons who assisted Amat Pakal and I will ask them whether
on the same understanding, they are willing also to make good
the additional $ 17.60.

R. M. J. Martin, Esquire,
Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
SHANGHAI.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,
〔此处转录不清〕
Consul-General.

先生：

谨此通知阁下，根据天津荷兰领事馆提交的关于遣返一名名为 Amat Pakal（别名 Doela Sanin）男子的往来信函，上海工部局似乎认为本人已对该人行使管辖权。就此，本人希望澄清，自始至终本人均拒绝这样做，本人对该人的关注仅限于向爪哇-中国-日本轮船公司（Java China Japan Line）当地管理处查询，他们是否能让此人登上其中一艘轮船并将其送得更靠近家乡。他们准备这样做，因此不存在本人曾命令遣返 Amat Pakal 的情况。他是经本人建议自愿离开的。正如随函附上的 Isemonger 先生致 Snyers 先生的信件副本所示，天津英国工部局乐意收回为此人花费的全部费用。

上海荷兰慈善会准备捐助 20 美元，前提是不损害该人的国籍身份，该款项已由本人汇往天津，用于偿还协助 Amat Pakal 的那些私人人士，本人将询问他们在同样前提下，是否也愿意补足额外的 17.60 美元。

R. M. J. Martin 先生，
警务处处长，
上海工部局，
上海。

谨致
敬礼，

〔此处转录不清〕
总领事。

COPIE

BRITISH MUNICIPAL COUNCIL.
Police Department.

Council Offices.
Tientsin, 7th October 1931.

Monsieur Snyers,

I forward for your information a copy
of a letter which I have received from the Commissioner
of Police, Shanghai, regarding the man Amat Pakal. I do
not know whether the Netherlands Consular Authorities at
Shanghai will be prepared to reimburse expenses incurred
here on this man's account, nor do I particularly press
that payment should be made, but in case you consider that
we can fairly claim repayment the following is an account
of expenditure.

Food from 4th August to 18th September
at 30 cents a day $ 13.80
Railway Fare to Tangku with escort 3.80
Steamer Fare to Shanghai 10.00
Subsistence Money 10.00

Total: $ 37.60

Of this you have already personnally contributed ten
dollars.

Yours Sincerely,
(signed) F. Isemonger.

Monsieur T. Snyers,
Belgian Consulate General,
TIENTSIN.
pages.zh:
副本

英国工部局。
警务部。

理事会办公室。
天津，1931年10月7日。

Snyers 先生：

现转呈一份上海警务处处长关于 Amat Pakal 男子的来信副本，供阁下参考。本人不知上海荷兰领事当局是否愿意报销在此地为此人产生的费用，本人也不特别坚持要求付款，但若阁下认为我们可以合理要求偿还，以下是支出账目。

8月4日至9月18日的伙食费
每天30分，共 13.80 美元
乘火车至塘沽并伴有护送人员 3.80 美元
至上海的轮船费 10.00 美元
生活津贴 10.00 美元

总计：37.60 美元

其中您个人已贡献十美元。

此致
敬礼，
（签名）F. Isemonger。

T. Snyers 先生，
比利时总领事馆，
天津。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
& S. L. REGISTRY
S. B. D. 2768.
Date 26. 9. 31.

September 25 31.

My dear Isemonger,

With reference to your letter of September
17, 1931, Amat Pakal arrived in Shanghai by the s.s.
"Pau Sang" on September 21, and was in accordance with
an order made by the Netherlands Consular Authorities
here repatriated to Sumatra by the s.s. "Tjisadane"
which sailed on September 24.

Amat Pakal, who appears to be mentally
deranged, when interviewed by the Shanghai Municipal
Police, gave his name as Doela Sanin, age 40. He
added that he was a native of Atje, Poloe Lombo,
Sumatra and that he had been in Tientsin for the past
nine months. Of the $10.00 which you gave him, he
spent $2 in Shanghai and the remaining $8.00 was
handed over to the Captain of the s.s. "Tjisadane" for
safe keeping.

Yours sincerely,

〔此处转录不清〕

F. Isemonger, Esq., C.I.E.,
Chief of Police,
British Municipal Council,
Tientsin.

〔签名〕

& S. L. 登记处
S. B. D. 2768.

1931年9月25日。

亲爱的 Isemonger：

关于阁下1931年9月17日的来信，Amat Pakal 于9月21日乘“Pau Sang”轮抵达上海，并根据此地荷兰领事当局的命令，于9月24日由“Tjisadane”轮遣返回苏门答腊。

Amat Pakal 似乎精神错乱，在接受上海公共租界工部局警务处问话时，自称名为 Doela Sanin，年龄40岁。他补充说自己是苏门答腊 Poloe Lombo 的 Atje 人，并已在天津待了九个月。在您给他的10.00美元中，他在上海花掉了2美元，剩余的8.00美元已交给“Tjisadane”轮船长保管。

此致
敬礼，

〔此处转录不清〕

F. Isemonger 先生，C.I.E.，
警察局长，
英国工部局，
天津。

〔签名〕

Date 22 / 9 / 31 Section 3, S.B. STATION
REPORT
Date Sept. 22, 1931.

Subject (in full) AMAT PAKAL

Made by D. S. Sansom. Forwarded by [Signature]

The above named person, the subject of the
attached correspondence, arrived in Shanghai from Tientsin
on the 21-9-31 on the S.S. 'Fau Sang', Jardine Matheson & Co.
Interrogated by the undersigned, he gave his
name as Doela Sanin, age 40, native of Atje, Poloe Lombo,
Sumatra. He also states that he has been in Tientsin
for the past 9 months, but he is unable to give any
particulars of his arrival there. Further questioning is
useless as it is evident that he is suffering from a mental
derangement.
The Netherlands Consul interviewed him on the
22.10.31, and, accepting jurisdiction, will arrange to
repatriate him to Sumatra as soon as possible. In the
meantime he is being detained at Central Station.
The sum of $10.00, the property of the above
named, was handed to the undersigned by the Captain of the
"Fau Sang" and has been deposited at Central Station.

[Signature]
D. S.

Officer i/c Special Branch.
S2, Please report again when he
has been repatriated.
D.S. Moore Mr. Van den Berg might assist.
SBR 22/9.
[Signature]

日期：1931年9月22日。

主题（全称）：AMAT PAKAL

制作人：D. S. Sansom。 转呈人 [签名]

上述人员，即附呈信函所涉及的对象，于1931年9月21日乘坐怡和洋行（Jardine Matheson & Co.）的“Fau Sang”轮从天津抵达上海。
经本人讯问，他自称名为 Doela Sanin，年龄40岁，籍贯为苏门答腊 Poloe Lombo 的 Atje。他还声称过去9个月一直在天津，但无法提供抵达那里的任何细节。进一步讯问已无用处，因为显然他患有精神错乱。
荷兰领事于1931年10月22日（原文如此，应为9月22日）对他进行了问话，并接受管辖权，将尽快安排将其遣返回苏门答腊。在此期间，他被拘押在中央巡捕房。
上述人员的财产，即10.00美元，已由“Fau Sang”轮船长交给本人，并存放在中央巡捕房。

[签名]
D. S.

特别分部主管警官。
S2，请在其被遣返后再次报告。
D.S. Moore Van den Berg 先生或许能提供协助。

17th. September, 1931.

My dear Quarton

I enclose a copy of a note written to the Agent
of Messrs. Jardine & Co. regarding a Malay, or native
of Sumatra who has been left behind by some steamer in
Tientsin, and who is destitute. I am sending him down
to Shanghai in the hope that he will be able to find a
fellow country man and assistance to get to his own country.
Can you help in the matter or get the Dutch Consular
authorities to do anything to assist.
The man has been given ten dollars to help him while
in Shanghai.

Yours Sincerely,

Major R. Martin
Commissioner of Police
Shanghai.

J. Seaman.

1931年9月17日。

亲爱的 Quarton：

随函附上一份写给怡和洋行代理人的便条副本，内容涉及一名马来人或苏门答腊土著，他被某艘轮船遗留在天津，且身无分文。我正将他送往上海，希望他能找到同胞并获得帮助回到自己的国家。
您能否在此事上提供帮助，或促使荷兰领事当局提供任何协助。
已给予该人十美元，以帮助他在上海期间的生活。

此致
敬礼，

R. Martin 少校
警务处处长
上海。

J. Seaman。

pages.en:
COPY.

16th. September, 1931.

Dear

On the 4th August a man, who apparently is either
Malay or a native of Sumatra was found in a destitute
condition on the Bund, and was brought into the Police
Station. After some time it was found that he under-
stood a little Dutch, and his name was ascertained to
be Amat Pakal. He claimed to be a resident of Madal,
Sumatra and it was presumed that he was a Dutch subject.
The Consul for the Netherlands was therefore asked to
make arrangements to send him back to his home. After
the lapse of some weeks the Consul decided that it was
impossible to prove the man's nationality and he was
therefore unable to undertake the responsibility of
repatriating him. Application was then made to the
British Consul who expressed his inability to do any-
thing. The only course remaining is to send the man
to the Chinese authorities with a request that they
should assist him. As this is unlikely to be produc-
tive of any result I write to ask you whether you will
allow the man to travel on one of your Steamers as a
deck passenger to Shanghai where he is more likely to
meet a fellow countryman and to receive assistance than
in Tientsin. Mr. Snyers, who is acting as Consul for
the Netherlands has agreed to join me in paying for
his passage and for his food, and to provide him with
pages.zh:
副本。

1931年9月16日。

亲爱的

8月4日，一名显然是马来人或苏门答腊土著的男子在外滩被发现时处于赤贫状态，并被带入巡捕房。过了一段时间，发现他懂一点荷兰语，并查明其名为 Amat Pakal。他声称是苏门答腊 Madal 的居民，因此推测他是荷兰臣民。于是请求荷兰领事安排将其送回家乡。几周后，领事决定无法证明该人的国籍，因此无法承担遣返他的责任。随后向英国领事提出申请，后者表示无能为力。剩下的唯一途径是将该人移交给中国当局，请求他们提供协助。鉴于这不太可能产生任何结果，我写信询问您是否允许该人作为甲板乘客乘坐您的一艘轮船前往上海，在那里他比在天津更有可能遇到同胞并获得援助。担任荷兰领事的 Snyers 先生已同意与我共同支付他的船费和伙食费，并为他提供

pages.en:
- 2 -

a little money.
    I should be grateful if you can assist me in this
case. The man apparently came here as a stoker on a
steamer and was either dumped ashore or missed his steamer
by some mishap. Being unable to speak any language but
his own and a little Dutch he is incapable of helping
himself.

                Yours faithfully,
                **〔此处转录不清〕**

J. C. Taylor Esquire,
Agent Messrs. Jardine Matheson & Co.
    Tientsin.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

少量金钱。
    若您能在此案中协助我，我将不胜感激。该人显然是作为轮船司炉工来到这里的，要么是被抛弃上岸，要么是因某种不幸错过了轮船。由于除了自己的语言和一些荷兰语外不会说其他语言，他无法自助。

                此致
                敬礼，
                **〔此处转录不清〕**

J. C. Taylor 先生，
怡和洋行代理人
    天津。
